triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: suspecting that she would go to Fyodor Pavlovitch in his absence, he returned at last to the town, to find, to his joy, that she had not been near his father.

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: Here Ippolit Kirillovitch described at length the prisoner’s fatal passion for Grushenka.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: At the same time the prisoner’s father was captivated by the same young person—a strange and fatal coincidence, for they both lost their hearts to her simultaneously, though both had known her before.

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: when he knelt before her, stretching out hands that were already stained with the blood of his father and rival.

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: that very three thousand roubles, which the son looked upon as his own property, part of his inheritance from his mother, of which his father was cheating him.

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: But note, frantic as he was, he took with him a brass pestle.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: The old man, who worshiped money, at once set aside three thousand roubles as a reward for one visit from her

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: And, in fact, from that letter we see that the whole fact of the murder was premeditated.

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: At this point Ippolit Kirillovitch broke off to discuss exhaustively the suspected connection of Smerdyakov with the murder.

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: and there learns that Smerdyakov is in a fit, that the other servant is ill—the coast is clear and he knows the ‘signals’

triples.subject: Grushenka
triples.quote: Had the maid told him that her mistress was at Mokroe with her former lover, nothing would have happened.
